0.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type V, also known as McArdle disease, is the entity in question. It was characterized in 1959 by W. F. H. M. Mommaerts and colleagues. McArdle disease is a metabolic myopathy resulting from a deficiency of myophosphorylase, the enzyme responsible for glycogen breakdown in muscle. It is included in the differential diagnosis for glycogen storage disease type III (Forbes-Cori disease) because both conditions involve abnormalities in glycogen metabolism, although they affect different tissues and enzymes.
0.short_answer: glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
